get.summary: Scaffold route, left public so you can check the server is up without a token.

post.summary:
`POST /auth/login`: exchanges an email and password for an access token.

`@Body()` hands over the request body as a `LoginDto`; Nest validates it first and
answers `400` itself if it is invalid. `@HttpCode(200)` is needed because Nest
answers `201 Created` to every POST by default, and a login creates nothing.

get.summary:
`GET /auth/me`: returns the user the token belongs to. The frontend calls it when the
page loads to check that a stored token is still valid and to learn who is logged in.

It has no `@Public()`, so JwtAuthGuard requires a valid token before this runs.
`@Roles` opens it to drivers too (routes are admin-only by default), and it works before
a forced password change, so the frontend can learn that the change is required.

post.summary:
`POST /auth/verify-email`: confirms the email address from the token in the welcome
email's link. Public: the driver cannot log in before this. `204` on success.

`POST /auth/change-password`: the logged-in user replaces their password. This is the
one action allowed while a temporary password must be changed. Returns the updated user.

requestBody.description: The website's application JSON (snake_case fields, values mostly strings). Required: request_id, first_name, last_name, email, phone. Other fields are kept as sent.

post.summary:
`POST /applications`: receives a driver application from the gonzocar.com form.

Public: applicants have no account. The body is typed `unknown` instead of a DTO class,
so the global ValidationPipe leaves it alone and ApplicationsService does the (lenient)
checks. Answers `201` with the same body for a new or a repeated submission.

get.summary:
`GET /applications`: one page of applications, newest first.

`@Query()` collects the query string into the DTO and validates it, the same way
`@Body()` does for a request body. An invalid value (e.g. `status=foo`) is a `400`.

parameters.name: startOnboarding
parameters.description:
`true` for "Add driver": after approving, also create the driver (in onboarding), so the admin lands on the
driver's page. Omitted or `false` for "Add application": approved only, no driver.

capital.description: Required, as an amount in USD, only when has_startup_funds is no

post.summary:
`POST /applications/manual`: an admin types in an application by hand, with its documents (D68). Same fields and
rules as the website form. It is approved straight away (D79). Approving creates no driver (D80): with
`?startOnboarding=true` ("Add driver") the driver is created too and the result carries its `driverId`; without
it ("Add application") `driverId` is null.
Admin only (no `@Public`). Multipart form data: the text fields plus the files `license_file` (required),
`rating_file` and `earnings_file` (JPG, PNG or PDF, at most 10 MB each). The file fields end in `_file` because
`earnings` is already a text field (weekly earnings).

The interceptor is multer, the library you would mount as `upload.fields([...])` in Express: it reads the
multipart body, keeps the files in memory and leaves the text fields in `@Body()`, where the global
ValidationPipe checks them against `ManualApplicationDto`.

`201` with `created: false` when the same `request_id` was already stored.

get.summary:
`GET /applications/approved`: the Approved applications page (D80): approved applications whose onboarding is not
finished (no driver yet, or the driver is still in onboarding), with the onboarding progress. Same search, dates and
`archived` switch as the main list. Declared before `:id` so "approved" is never read as an id.

post.summary:
`POST /applications/bulk-delete`: deletes applications for good, with their documents and (when no one else
uses the phone) their text history (B66). All or nothing: `409` if any is approved, and then nothing is
deleted. Unknown ids are ignored.

POST with a body rather than DELETE: a DELETE request with a body is poorly supported by proxies and HTTP
clients. Declared before `:id` routes so "bulk-delete" is never read as an id (it is also a POST, so it
could not clash with `GET :id` anyway).

get.summary:
`GET /applications/:id`: one application with its full details.

`ParseUUIDPipe` rejects an id that is not a UUID with `400` before any query runs
(Postgres would otherwise fail on it with a 500). A valid but unknown id is a `404`.

post.summary:
`POST /applications/:id/approve`: marks the application approved, texts the applicant and starts onboarding (creates
the driver, B116). Optional body `{ "message": "..." }` is the approval text the admin picked and edited (B81); without
it the first approved template is sent. `{ "sendText": false }` approves without any text (B111). `400` for an
unknown placeholder in it.

POST because it is an action with side effects, not an edit of a field. `@HttpCode(200)`
because it returns the updated application rather than creating a resource at this URL.

`POST /applications/:id/reject`: declines the application (shown as "Declined", B69). No driver is created.
Optional body `{ "message": "..." }` texts the applicant that declined text, as the admin picked and edited
it (B72, B81); without a message nothing is sent. `503` if the text could not be sent (then nothing is declined).
`POST /applications/:id/hold`: puts the application on hold to decide later.

`POST /applications/:id/start-onboarding`: for an approved application, creates the driver (in onboarding) and
their login (D80). `409` if it is not approved, is archived, already has its driver, or a driver or login already
has this email.

`POST /applications/:id/archive`: hides the application from the normal list (D80); delete stays separate. Its
driver, whatever the status, is archived with it (D84), which stops billing and reminders.
`POST /applications/:id/unarchive`: brings an archived application (and its driver, D84) back.

get.summary: `GET /applications/:id/documents`: the files, as our own copies (D54) or admin uploads (D68).

put.summary:
`PUT /applications/:id/documents/:kind`: puts one file (multipart field `file`) in the licence, rating or earnings
slot, replacing what is there, a website copy included (D68). JPG, PNG or PDF, at most 10 MB; `400` otherwise.
Returns the slot. PUT because the slot ends up holding exactly this file however many times it is sent.

get.summary: `GET /drivers/:id/documents`: the driver's files, each with a short-lived link to open it.

put.summary:
`PUT /drivers/:id/documents/:kind`: puts one file (multipart field `file`) in the licence, rating, earnings or
contract slot, replacing what is there. The contract (D90) is always kept on the driver itself. JPG, PNG or PDF,
at most 10 MB; `400` otherwise. Returns the slot.

post.summary:
`POST /sms/:kind/:id/messages`: sends a text, according to SMS_MODE.
`409` texting is off, `502` Quo refused (the failure is saved and shown in the chat),
`400` the application's phone is not a US number, `404` unknown record.
`POST /sms/:kind/:id/sync`: pulls this contact's history from Quo (texts sent from the Quo app too).

`GET /message-templates`: every template, grouped by kind, with its placeholders and last edit.

post.summary: `POST /message-templates`: adds a template. `400` empty, too long or unknown placeholder; `409` name taken.

put.summary:
`PUT /message-templates/:id`: replaces a template's name and text. PUT because both are replaced. `400` empty,
too long or unknown placeholder; `404` unknown id; `409` name taken.

delete.summary: `DELETE /message-templates/:id`: `404` unknown id; `409` if it is the last template of its kind.

get.summary: `GET /ledger-presets`: every preset, charges first, each kind in the order of its cards.

post.summary: `POST /ledger-presets`: adds a preset at the end of its kind. `400` bad amount or text; `409` name taken.

put.summary:
`PUT /ledger-presets/order`: sets the order of one kind's cards (`kind`, `ids` = all that kind's ids). `400` the ids
are not exactly that kind's presets. Declared before `:id` so "order" is never read as an id.

`PUT /ledger-presets/:id`: replaces a preset's name, amount and description (PUT because all three are replaced; the
amount may be null). `400` bad amount or text; `404` unknown id; `409` name taken.

delete.summary: `DELETE /ledger-presets/:id`: `404` unknown id. Entries made from it keep their text and amount.

post.summary: `POST /contracts/calculate`: the numbers for some inputs, nothing saved. `400` bad inputs.

get.summary: `GET /contracts/companies`: the fixed list of companies a contract's Lessor is chosen from (not paginated: five rows).
`GET /contracts/vehicles`: the business's vehicles to pick on the Vehicle card (B120; not paginated: about 40).

post.summary:
`POST /drivers/:driverId/contract/licence-details`: reads address, licence number, state and date of birth from the
driver's licence file with the AI (B121, D86). Nothing is saved: the page puts the values in the draft's boxes.
POST because every call asks the AI again. `404` unknown driver, `409` no licence on file or none found in it,
`502` the AI or the bucket failed, `503` the AI is not set up.

get.summary: `GET /drivers/:driverId/contract`: the open draft or else the contract sent last, or `{ contract: null }`. `404` unknown driver.

post.summary: `POST /drivers/:driverId/contracts`: starts the draft. `400` bad inputs or unknown company; `404` unknown driver; `409` a draft exists.

put.summary: `PUT /contracts/:id`: replaces every input of a draft. `400` bad inputs or unknown company; `404` unknown id or not a draft.

delete.summary: `DELETE /contracts/:id`: deletes a draft. `404` unknown id or not a draft.

post.summary:
`POST /contracts/:id/send`: sends the draft to the driver to sign (firma) and freezes it. `400` values still empty
(`missing`); `404` unknown id; `409` already sent, or its company's state has no contract yet; `502` firma refused; `503` no firma key.

get.summary:
`GET /contracts/:id/documents`: short-lived links to the signed contract and its certificate (D75), minted for this
request and never stored. Both are null until the files are saved. `404` unknown id.

parameters.name: onboarding
parameters.description:
`false` leaves out drivers still in `onboarding`: the Drivers page lists only active and inactive drivers, those
in onboarding are on the Approved applications page (D80). Omitted or `true`: every status, which is what the
payment pickers need (a deposit arrives while the driver is still in onboarding).

parameters.name: collections
parameters.description:
`true` lists only drivers in collections (D81), newest sent first, and the date range then filters the day they
were sent. `false` leaves them out: the Drivers page, since they are on the Collections page. Omitted: no
collections filter, which is what the payment pickers need (money from a driver in collections must still be
assignable to them).

parameters.name: withoutApplication
parameters.description:
`true` lists only drivers with no application: the ones an admin added directly (D85). With `status=onboarding` it
is the Drivers page's "Onboarding (added directly)" view; a driver in onboarding who came from an application is
on the Approved applications page instead. Omitted or `false`: no filter.

get.summary: `GET /drivers`: one page of drivers, newest first.

rentDueTime.description: Time rent is due, Chicago time, HH:MM (24 hours)

post.summary:
`POST /drivers`: an admin adds a driver directly, without an application (D85). Multipart form data: the text fields
(name, email and phone are required; the profile and `aliases`, a JSON list of `{type, value}`, are optional) and the
optional files `licenseFile` and `earningsFile` (JPG, PNG or PDF, at most 10 MB each). The driver starts in
onboarding with no login, and nothing is texted. `409` when a driver already has the email, or an alias
already belongs to another driver; nothing is saved then. Answers with the new driver.

The interceptor is multer, the library you would mount as `upload.fields([...])` in Express: it reads the multipart
body, keeps the files in memory and leaves the text fields in `@Body()`, where the global ValidationPipe checks them.

get.summary: `GET /drivers/:id`: one driver. `400` for a malformed id, `404` if unknown.

patch.summary:
`PATCH /drivers/:id/profile`: changes the profile fields (middle name, address, date of birth, insurance, D85). A
field left out stays; one sent empty is cleared. Returns the updated driver.

`PATCH /drivers/:id/rent-settings`: changes the time of day rent is due (Chicago time, `HH:MM`) and the "On Payment
Plan" flag (D92). A field left out stays; `rentDueTime: null` clears it. Returns the updated driver. `400` for a bad
time, `404` if unknown.

post.summary:
`POST /drivers/:id/onboarding`: ticks or un-ticks one onboarding step (D56). The driver becomes `active` when
the third step is ticked, and goes back to `onboarding` when one is un-ticked. Returns the updated driver.
`409` if the driver is inactive.

`POST /drivers/:id/aliases`: adds a payment alias (a name or handle the driver pays from, per payment method) so
their payments match automatically (D69). `409` with the owner's name when another driver already has it.
Returns the updated driver.

delete.summary: `DELETE /drivers/:id/aliases/:aliasId`: removes one of the driver's aliases. Returns the updated driver.

post.summary:
`POST /drivers/:id/deactivate`: the driver left (B67), and how: `reason` is required (D81). Their login stops
working at once.

`POST /drivers/:id/collections`: sends the driver to collections (D81). `reason` is needed when no reason is noted
yet; the driver is then deactivated in the same step. `409` for a driver still in onboarding.
`POST /drivers/:id/remove-from-collections`: takes the driver out of collections; they stay inactive.

`POST /drivers/:id/archive`: hides the driver from the normal list and stops billing and reminders (D80). Any
driver, no need to deactivate first; drivers are archived, never deleted. The application they came from is
archived with them (D84).
`POST /drivers/:id/unarchive`: brings an archived driver back, with the status they had, and their application with them (D84).
`POST /drivers/:id/reactivate`: back to `active` (all steps done) or `onboarding`; login works again.

credit applied against a charge (`appliesToId`). `201` the entry (also when the same `requestKey` is sent
again); `400` invalid amount, date or direction, or more than is left on the charge; `404` unknown driver or
charge; `409` the key reused for a different entry.

get.summary: `GET /payments`: one page of payments, most recent first. `?match=review` lists "Needs review".

post.summary:
`POST /payments/manual`: records a payment an admin received by hand (cash, check, card, or any method) and
credits the driver's ledger. `201` the payment (also when the same `requestKey` is sent again); `400` bad
amount or date, unknown driver; `409` a possible duplicate (body has `code: "possible_duplicate"` and the
payment found; send `confirmDuplicate: true` to record anyway), the key reused, or the reference used before.

`POST /payments/:id/void`: voids a payment recorded by hand and reverses its ledger credit. `201` the payment;
`404` unknown payment; `409` not a manual payment, or already voided.

`POST /payments/:id/assign`: assigns or re-assigns a payment to a driver and saves the payer's name as
that driver's alias (unless another driver already owns it, which the answer reports).
`404` unknown payment, `400` unknown driver, `409` a rejected or discrepancy payment.

info.title: GonzoCar API
info.description: Admin and driver API for the GonzoCar platform.

password.description: The account's password, in plain text (it only travels over HTTPS in production).

mustChangePassword.description:
True while the user still has a system-generated password. Until they change it, every
endpoint except `GET /auth/me` and `POST /auth/change-password` answers `403`.

accessToken.description: Signed token the client sends back on every request as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

token.description: The `token` from the verification link in the welcome email.

currentPassword.description: The password the user logs in with now (the temporary one, at first login).

newPassword.description:
The new password: at least 8 characters. The 72-byte limit (bcrypt) is checked by the
service, since characters outside English can take more than one byte.

application_id.description: Our id for the application. A repeated submission (same `request_id`) gets the same id.

created.description: False when the same `request_id` had already been stored (a double click or a retry): nothing new was made.

driverId.description:
The driver created by approving it (D79). Null only for a repeat of a request whose approval has not finished, or
whose application an admin has since declined or put on hold.

phone.description: As the applicant typed it (usually 10 digits).

submittedAt.description: When the applicant pressed submit, by their browser's clock.

alertError.description: Why the alert text to staff about this application could not be sent; null if it did not fail.

archivedAt.description: When an admin archived it (D80); null = not archived.

driverStatus.description: Status of the driver "Start onboarding" created (D80); null if there is none. Archiving also archives that driver (D84).

total.description: Number of applications matching the filter, across all pages.

status.description: `onboarding` here by definition: a driver who is `active` or `inactive` is on the Drivers page.

contractSignedAt.description: The three onboarding steps (D56): when each was ticked; null while not done.

phone.description: As the applicant typed it (usually 10 digits).

submittedAt.description: When the applicant pressed submit, by their browser's clock.

alertError.description: Why the alert text to staff about this application could not be sent; null if it did not fail.

archivedAt.description: When an admin archived it (D80); null = not archived.

driverStatus.description: Status of the driver "Start onboarding" created (D80); null if there is none. Archiving also archives that driver (D84).

driver.description: Null until an admin presses "Start onboarding"; then the driver, while onboarding is not finished.

ids.description: The applications to delete. Ids that no longer exist are ignored.

filesNotRemoved.description:
Copied files (documents, texted-in files) that could not be removed from the bucket. The database rows are
gone either way; the reason for each is in the server log. 0 when everything was removed.

phone.description: As the applicant typed it (usually 10 digits).

submittedAt.description: When the applicant pressed submit, by their browser's clock.

alertError.description: Why the alert text to staff about this application could not be sent; null if it did not fail.

archivedAt.description: When an admin archived it (D80); null = not archived.

driverStatus.description: Status of the driver "Start onboarding" created (D80); null if there is none. Archiving also archives that driver (D84).

requestId.description: The website's id for the submission.

licenseStoragePath.description: Paths in the client's Supabase `driver-documents` bucket.

payload.description: The full submission as the website sent it, minus the bot-check token.

reviewedById.description: The admin who last reviewed it. Null while pending.

driverId.description: The driver created by "Start onboarding" (D80). Null until then, and always null unless approved.

alertedAt.description: When the alert text to staff was really sent; null if it was not (off, dry run, or failed).

createdBy.description: The admin who added it by hand (D68). Null for applications that came from the website form.

sendText.description: `false` approves without texting the applicant (`message` is then ignored). Default `true`.

message.description:
The text, with `{firstName}` / `{lastName}` placeholders (filled in by the API; unknown ones are refused, 400).
1 to 1000 characters after trimming. Approve without it sends the first approved template; decline without it
sends no text.

The text, with `{firstName}` / `{lastName}` placeholders (filled in by the API; unknown ones are refused, 400).
1 to 1000 characters after trimming. Approve without it sends the first approved template; decline without it

balanceCents.description: Ledger balance in cents: credits minus debits; negative = the driver owes.

daysLate.description: Whole days the oldest late rent payment is late (Chicago clock); 0 when the reason is the deposit only.

depositDaysSinceDue.description: Days since the unpaid deposit was due (the contract start date); null when the deposit is not what is unpaid.

depositCents.description: The unpaid deposit in cents; null when the deposit is not what is unpaid.

totalCents.description: Confirmed payments that came in that week, in cents; 0 for a quiet week.

amountCents.description: The amount typed when the step was ticked (D82), in cents; null for a step ticked before amounts were recorded.

totalCents.description: The recorded amounts added up, in cents.

withoutAmountCount.description: How many drivers have no amount recorded; they are in the list and not in the total.

amountCents.description: The deposit the signed contract asks for, in cents.

dueDate.description: The day it is due: the contract start date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

daysSinceDue.description: Days since the due date; negative before it.

overdue.description: 7 or more days since the due date: the driver is also on the Should Be Deactivated list (unless on a payment plan).

DriverLeftReason.description: How the driver left (D81); null for a driver deactivated before reasons existed.

leftReason.description: How the driver left (D81); null for a driver deactivated before reasons existed.

balanceCents.description: Ledger balance in cents: credits minus debits; negative = the driver owes.

sentToCollectionsAt.description: When an admin sent the driver to collections.

totalOwedCents.description: What is owed by the drivers in the list (only the ones with a negative balance count), in cents.

asOf.description: When the figures were worked out.

dueToday.description: Payments due today: weekly drivers first, then daily, then by name.

late.description: Drivers with a late rent payment, the longest late first.

earlyWarning.description: Drivers whose oldest late payment is a full day or more late, the longest late first.

shouldBeDeactivated.description: Drivers who meet a deactivation rule and are not on a payment plan, the longest overdue first. List only.

weeks.description: The current week and the 25 before it, newest first (D5). Monday to Sunday, Chicago days.

periodStart.description: First Chicago day of the period (the 1st, a Monday, or the day itself), `YYYY-MM-DD`.

periodEnd.description: Last Chicago day of the period (the end of the month, a Sunday, or the day itself).

totalCents.description: Confirmed payments received in the period, in cents. 0 for a quiet period.

paymentCount.description: How many confirmed payments that is.

total.description: How many periods there are in all, so the page count can be worked out.

totalCents.description: Confirmed payments in the whole filter (every period, every page), in cents.

paymentCount.description: How many confirmed payments that is.

archived.description: An archived driver is listed too: money received stays revenue (D93).

totalCents.description: Confirmed payments received from them in the filter, in cents.

paymentCount.description: How many confirmed payments that is.

lastPaymentAt.description: When the latest of those payments was received.

total.description: How many drivers have at least one payment in the filter.

totalCents.description: Confirmed payments of every driver in the filter, in cents (the same figure as the collections total).
